body: The seam's closed request set grows by exactly two: the monitors query and one move-to-workspace dispatch. Each has a closed argv builder and a closed parse. Any request beyond these two is an operator fork, written and stopped on.
Reply text is dropped at the parse except what a closed per-request keep-list names, so no hyprctl reply text travels past the seam. Peer replies are screened down to closed code words.
The closed error words stay as they are. A new closed word is an operator fork, not something the chunk adds. Unlisted code words are not coined to cover the new requests.
The move dispatch's argv takes only a validated window address and an integer workspace, and is never an exec. Its exact form on Hyprland 0.56.2 is what R1 measures.

The hyprctl read deadline is settled at 5 s by the operator's answer. It is a time bound on the driver (the read of a compositor reply), never on a human, and the human sees no timeout from it because the seam has no product caller.
A test times a real read against the 5 s deadline, not the short read_within bound the current deadline test uses. A time bound beyond the settled 5 s is an operator fork.
The drain cap gets a witness: a test drives the read's own stdout drain past MAX_FRAME. It replaces the parse test the hyprctl reply Boundary row names today.

The tap records monitors read-only with no window (R3, allowed in implement). The R1 window verb opens one foot window with no claude in it, moves it once, ends exactly the foot pid it started and leaves only fixture files. It runs only at R1, at a moment the operator names.

The fake agent standing as hyprctl replays the new requests by exact argv in each of its replay modes (recorded, oversize, malformed, absent), so tests reach the seam through recorded fixtures and never through a live compositor.

Live readings never gate: R1 and R3 are measurements that write fixtures. CI and the tests run against recorded fixtures only, and the chunk's wrap waits for R1 without any test depending on a live window.

The seam stays an internal crate with no product caller, a root dev-dependency only. The carve-out that internal crates are not assertable for accessibility applies, so no output-discipline assertions are owed for the new requests.
Invariants of the new requests, the deadline and the drain are held in crate tests that the mutation audit would cover. This phase itself runs no mutation tier.

This phase makes no live start, opens, moves, focuses or closes no window, sends no key, runs no mutation tier and calls no timer tool. The only allowed live call is a read-only compositor query that dispatches nothing.

body: The seam's closed request set grows by two: a `monitors` query and one move-to-workspace dispatch; each closed request, its closed argv and its closed words change only by a recorded decision, and nothing outside the two enters.
The move dispatch's argv takes only a validated window address and an integer workspace; no free text, no exec form reaches it.
The `monitors` parse drops all reply text save what its closed keep-list names, and is held as a parser surface by property tests over its input.
Every external reader is bounded and keeps the frame cap: the hyprctl read's own stdout drain is driven past MAX_FRAME by a bounded remove-the-guard witness, not by a parse test.
The read deadline is one product constant, settled at 5 s; the test that times a read against it takes the constant from the product, never a copy, and waits without sleep synchronisation or retries.

The fake agent serves the hyprctl boundary as a real stub executable on a test-scoped PATH, replaying recorded bytes by exact argv; the new requests get replay cases in its recorded, oversize, malformed and absent modes, and the fake stays held to the recorded fixtures byte for byte.

New hyprctl fixtures are recorded by the test-only tap from a real run, per compositor version, never hand-written, scrubbed of home paths and usernames, and pass the fixture hygiene walk and schema check.
The tap is a test-only binary in the one test-only workspace member; no test-only binary reaches a release build.
The R1 window verb is a live reading: run only locally at the operator's host, never in CI and never from a test; what it gives is recorded as a reading, never as verification.
The tap ends only the foot window it started: the pid and start time it spawned are verified before the kill, and it is told apart from standing windows; it leaves only fixture files.
No test or tap reads the operator's real claude sessions or home; every test runs in its own fresh home.
Mocks only at product seams: the Hyprland seam is tested against the real stub process and real files, with no mock library over hyprctl.
Seam errors stay in the closed error word set and carry no path or upstream reply text.
